clue.text: University lacking in perception first to decline judgment

indicators.note: first says the word for decline goes at the front of the build

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline

indicators.note: lacking in says one letter is missing from the word for perception

parts.note: acuity is sharpness of perception

explanation.surface: A university short on insight is first to turn down a ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in' removes U from ACUITY, leaving ACITY; 'first' puts SAG ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sound judgment and wisdom are what this word names.

clue.text: Disgust resulting from away goal

parts.note: off means away, as in 'off to town'
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Fans are disgusted by a goal scored by the away side.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to disgust someone is to affront or upset them.

clue.text: Sailor turning West across his vessel?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: turning says the name is read backwards

parts.note: Mae West, the American actress

explanation.surface: A sailor turns west and looks across his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a compass point but is the actress Mae West.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term: at right angles to a ship's keel, i.e. straight across it.

clue.text: Projectile from lake is found in sea

indicators.note: found in says the lake letter plus 'is' sit inside the sea

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A projectile from a lake turns up in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: relating to projectiles, as in a missile travelling under gravity.

clue.text: Unmethodical toys ruled out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Toys are ruled out because play with them is aimless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking plan or purpose, random and haphazard.

clue.text: Put away ball, cutting forcefully

indicators.note: cutting means the ball shape slices into the word for forcefully

parts.note: hard means forcefully, as in 'hit hard'
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A tennis player puts the ball away, slicing it with force.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stash or store something up for later use.

clue.text: Easy-going relative given the push

parts.note: to be given the push is to be sacked, axed

explanation.surface: A laid-back relation has been sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: calm, informal and unworried in manner.

clue.text: Retired medical practitioner's still content

indicators.note: Retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
content means what is held inside these words, so the letters are found within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A retired doctor is calmly content.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'still content' as the definition, but 'content' signals the hidden letters (what the words contain); 'still' alone is the definition. Reading 'meDICAL Practitioner' backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: calm and undisturbed, as still water is.

clue.text: Pulped dessert to consume ordered from time to time

indicators.note: to consume says the dessert swallows the letters taken

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

indicators.note: from time to time means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dessert to be eaten is ordered every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' picks R, E, E from 'ordered'; 'to consume' puts them inside PUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mashed to a smooth pulp, as baby food is.

clue.text: Tinker getting last of tasty dishes, perhaps

parts.note: to tinker is to potter about doing small jobs

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tinker gets the last of some tasty dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: plates and bowls are typical ceramic ware, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Silent bird trapping bill

indicators.note: trapping says the bird holds the bill inside it

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A quiet bird has caught hold of a beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' suggests a beak beside 'bird', but it is AC, an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: understood or implied without being spoken.

clue.text: Commercial breaks less fraught for singer in evening

indicators.note: breaks says the commercial splits the comparative word open

parts.note: serener means calmer, less fraught
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Commercial breaks are less stressful for an evening singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: one who sings a serenade, traditionally at night beneath a window.

clue.text: Force trained up, expending energy for new form of attack

indicators.note: to force something is to wrench it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
expending says the energy letter is given up
for says the new letter takes its place

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Troops trained up, spending their energy on a new kind of assault.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap E for N in TRAINEDUP and rearrange. Tip-and-run is a cricket game where batters must run whenever the ball is hit, and also a raid of strike-and-flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a hit-and-flee raid, striking quickly then withdrawing.

clue.text: A chief with great strength, once

parts.note: main means chief, principal

explanation.surface: A leader with mighty power in days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic adverb: with full force, at full speed; 'once' flags it as old.

clue.text: Obscure female, one with two daughters to accommodate

indicators.note: to accommodate says the female houses the other letters

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
I is the Roman numeral one
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two of them give DD

explanation.surface: An unknown woman takes in a single parent of two girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: concealed or out of sight, unknown.

clue.text: Virgin taking off after scene

indicators.note: after says the minus word follows the scene word

parts.note: a spot is a place or scene
less means minus, with something taken off

explanation.surface: A Virgin flight takes off after the scene is set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' suggests the airline beside 'taking off'; it is the adjective meaning pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pure and unblemished, untouched, as virgin snow.

clue.text: The usual colours

definitions.meaning: the norm, the ordinary level or yardstick
a flag or banner, as regimental colours

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an accepted norm, and a military flag or ensign.

clue.text: Grand means of viewing Scottish lowlands?

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
a lens is a means of viewing

explanation.surface: A grand way of seeing the Scottish lowlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the Lowlands region: these are valleys, low land between hills, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: narrow Scottish valleys, lying low between the hills.

clue.text: Grammar term from Oedipus's bird?

parts.note: the Oedipus complex is Freud's term
bird is British slang for a prison sentence (birdlime, time)

explanation.surface: A grammar term derived from Oedipus's bird?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British rhyming slang for time inside (birdlime), i.e. a sentence; Oedipus lends Freud's complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar: a statement with a main clause and at least one subordinate clause.

clue.text: Mirror for one, old and a bit cracked

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mirror, old and slightly cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British popular daily newspaper, not a looking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Daily Mirror is a red-top popular paper of small page format.

clue.text: Hostess, say, needing someone present below stairs

indicators.note: below says, in a down clue, the second word sits under the first

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs
an attendant is someone who attends, is present

explanation.surface: A hostess needs a servant present downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below stairs' suggests domestic servants; it is FLIGHT with ATTENDANT under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an air hostess was the old name for cabin crew.

clue.text: Chance to resolve deadlock that prison rioters may be given?

definitions.meaning: added play in a drawn match, as in football

definitions.text: that prison rioters may be given?
definitions.meaning: an additional spell of jail time as punishment

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: added minutes to settle a drawn game, and a longer prison stay.

clue.text: Interpret letter describing how goods may be delivered

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so the letter word encloses the delivery term

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
COD, cash on delivery

explanation.surface: Reading a letter that explains delivery terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to work out the meaning of a coded message.

clue.text: Turn the spotlight on drama at college

parts.note: a play is a drama
up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Stage lighting for a student drama production.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to emphasise or highlight something.

clue.text: Origin of long journey Spooner's pot boy makes

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words swap places

parts.note: a pot is a paunch, a belly
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A pot boy starts out on a long trip, in Spooner's words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot boy' looks like a tavern lad; it is PAUNCH and LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the platform a rocket leaves from on a voyage into space.

clue.text: Water sources running dry in county

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters go inside the county

parts.note: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

indicators.note: running means the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Water supplies run dry in a county.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: street fire plugs that supply water for firefighters.

clue.text: Limits of destitute father's aspiration

indicators.note: limits means the outermost letters of the next word

parts.note: a sire is a father; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: The extent of a destitute father's hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a longing or wish for something.

clue.text: Talk up bargain veg

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rap is talk, chat
a snip is a bargain

explanation.surface: Talking up a cheap vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Output from sewer long undermining roadway

indicators.note: undermining says, in a down clue, the long word goes under the road word

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
to itch is to long for

explanation.surface: Output from a drain, a long stretch under the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' is not a drain: it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a single loop of thread made by one who sews.

clue.text: Adventurer from Harrow died, coming north

indicators.note: coming north says, in a down clue, the died letter rises above the harrow word

parts.note: a rake is a harrow, a tool for breaking soil

explanation.surface: An explorer from Harrow school dies on a trip north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrow' suggests the London school; it is a garden tool. Sir Francis Drake was an Elizabethan seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Francis Drake, the Elizabethan explorer and privateer.
